tob-10827: The Secret Doctrine is Helena Blavatsky’s massive masterwork, the cornerstone of Theosophy. This first volume, Cosmogenesis, sets out her account of the universe’s origin — vast cycles of creation, seven root races, and the spiritual evolution of humanity. Dense and controversial, it influenced occultists, artists, and thinkers for generations.
tob-4027: Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s Social Contract asks by what right anyone rules anyone — and answers that true rule rests only on the shared will of the people. The Discourses trace how high living warped man’s native goodness. These fiery ideas helped set off the French Revolution.
tob-4127: Franz Cumont’s classic study shows how Rome’s old gods yielded to the East’s mystery faiths — Isis, Mithras, Cybele, and lastly Christ. He tracks the rites, the won-over, and the hunger for a savior that remade the ancient world. The book redrew our map of Rome’s faith-revolution.
tob-0127: These opened FBI files log COINTELPRO’s ‘White Hate’ drive — the Bureau’s watch-and-wreck work against the Ku Klux Klan and fellow white-race gangs in the 1960s. Memos bare stool-pigeons, wiretaps, and dirty tricks. The papers show the FBI fighting home-bred terror by hook or crook.
tob-13527: 3 Enoch — the Hebrew Enoch-book — is the great Throne-seers’ writ, telling how Enoch rose through the heavens to stand as the angel Metatron. This Jewish inward-work shaped Kabbalah’s angel-teaching. The text is the heart of early Jewish inwardness-study.
cia-0000119727: A September 1956 report on the readmission of ex-premier Imre Nagy to the Hungarian party. Nagy, purged for reformism, was the hero the revolution would soon demand as leader. His return to the party was the first step toward his tragic destiny — premier of a revolt Moscow would crush.
cia-0000124327: A June 1952 survey of prisoner-of-war camps in North Korea and China. By mid-war, the camp system was mapped in outline — locations, populations, conditions. The document is the POW atlas taking shape: the geography of captivity, drawn from fragments.
cia-0000132427: A January 1960 report that Cuba was getting little official support for its proposed hungry nations conference — the archive's spelling says HungryY. Castro's Third World summitry found few takers. The document is a diplomatic flop, filed: the revolution's invitations, declined.
cia-0000132627: A June 1960 report: the USSR exploiting the Cuban situation. Moscow was working the crisis for every advantage — bases, prestige, leverage. The document is the exploitation: the superpower, profiting.

arxiv-2605-09027: Teams of AI agents can be attacked as a group — one compromised member poisons the rest. Alexandre Le Mercier, Chris Develder, and Thomas Demeester introduce Gambit, a three-mode benchmark for adversarial robustness in multi-agent LLM collectives. The 2026 paper stress-tests AI teamwork under fire.
arxiv-2605-09527: Batteries store energy in chemistry; a quantum capacitor would store it in quantum coherence — fragile, powerful, and strange. Saeed Haddadi proposes exactly such a device, a coherence-based quantum energy storage unit. The 2026 paper is quantum thermodynamics: a battery made of superpositions.
arxiv-2605-09727: In-context reinforcement learning that generalizes across domains might need non-linear transformers rather than the usual linear kind. Bowen He, Juncheng Dong, Lin Lin, and Xiang Cheng propose one architecture for all domains. The 2026 paper is about transformers that travel well between worlds.
plos-pone-0003427: Genome scientists rebuilt a pathogen's instruction book in this 2008 paper. Francisella tularensis, the highly infectious bacterium behind tularemia, had a genome assembly with errors, so the team re-assembled the OSU18 strain's sequence. The cleaner genome gives biodefense and infectious-disease researchers a trustworthy map for studying how this dangerous microbe works.
plos-pone-0003527: Geneticists found the sleeping-sickness parasite guarding its disguise factories in this 2008 paper. Trypanosoma brucei hides from immunity by cycling surface coats, and the telomeric expression sites controlling that switch turned out to be highly conserved. Their stability, despite sitting in mutation-prone chromosome ends, hints at how essential the disguise system is.
plos-pone-0003627: Bone researchers Roato, D'Amelio, and Gorassini found destroyers active in building-type metastases in this 2008 paper. Prostate cancer's bone-forming lesions were thought to be all builders, but osteoclasts, the bone-dissolving cells, proved active within them. The surprise implicates the full remodeling crew in the disabling bone damage of advanced disease.
plos-pone-0003727: In 2008, Sun, Skogerbø, and Wang studied DNA's most guarded stretches. Highly conserved elements, sequences barely changed across vertebrate evolution, were mapped against nearby genes to find structural relationships. The layout hints at why evolution froze these regions: they likely control the genes beside them.
plos-pone-0003827: A 2008 methods paper offered an endless cloning kit for gene-silencing work. The expandable strategy plus repeat-proof PCR lets labs build vectors carrying many shRNA pieces without the usual assembly headaches. The method removes a bottleneck from large-scale gene knockdown studies.
plos-pone-0003927: In 2008, Sernandez, de Yebenes, and Dorsett found half a gene dose mattering. Losing one copy of activation-induced deaminase, or AID, weakened antibody diversification. The same shortfall raised the risk of chromosome translocations, a cancer trigger. The haploinsufficiency shows antibody-shaping enzymes need their full strength.
plos-pone-0004027: In 2008, Wang, Xiao, and Pan surveyed the microbial world's tiniest proteins. Their systematic census covered mini-proteins, under one hundred amino acids, in bacteria and archaea. The tiny polypeptides proved ubiquitous and functionally important across all microbial life. The survey finally gives small proteins their due in biology's big picture.
plos-pone-0004127: In 2009, Richer, Lavallee, and Shanina found a viral alarm that saves lives. Toll-like receptor 3 signaling on macrophages proved vital against Coxsackievirus B4. Without TLR3, the infected mice quickly died. The receptor's early warning keeps the virus firmly in check.
plos-pone-0004227: In 2009, a US team built a focus test for mice. The 5-choice nonstop performance test gauged mouse watchfulness quite well. The task brings human attention testing to lab rodents. The handy tool aids drug screens for human thinking disorders today.
plos-pone-0004327: In 2009, van der Laan, de Kloet, and Meijer found timing ruling stress control. Glucocorticoid receptor repression of the CRH gene depended on precise timing. The receptor's silencing worked only in a tight window. The finding refines stress-hormone feedback models greatly.
plos-pone-0357227: The chemo drug cyclophosphamide saves cancer patients but poisons their kidneys. This lab study tested protodioscin — a plant compound — on human kidney cells exposed to the drug. The compound eased renal toxicity by calming endoplasmic reticulum stress, boosting antioxidant defenses, and slowing cell death — a promising lead for protecting kidneys during chemo.
plos-pone-0358627: Journals issue an Expression of Concern when a published paper’s reliability comes under question. This entry flags a paper on health risks from iron in wastewater-irrigated crops near Sargodha, Pakistan. The notice warns readers the findings are under review — a placeholder in the library until the investigation resolves.
plos-pone-0358327: Scientists cite papers to build on them, to refute them, or just to nod along. This data-driven study compared citation intents across scientific disciplines. The disciplinary patterns reveal how different fields actually use each other’s work — credit, critique, or courtesy.
plos-pone-0358227: Translating Confucius consistently across languages is a profound challenge spanning millennia. This paper used concept-aware contrastive representation learning for cross-translation semantic consistency modeling of the Analects. The AI approach keeps the sage’s meaning stable across tongues, catching drift that human translators miss.
plos-pone-0358427: The antibiotic levofloxacin can rupture tendons — but the risk isn’t equal for everyone. This disproportionality analysis using the FAERS and JADER adverse-event databases broke tendon disorder risk down by sex, age, and administration route. The patterns sharpen the warning for the patients most at risk.
plos-pone-0354427: Paddleboard athletes need calm, unshakeable focus on open water. This correlational study linked trait mindfulness, psychological skills, and mental toughness in paddleboard athletes. The connections reveal which mental training ingredients matter most when balance and composure decide the race.
plos-pone-0353827: Depression changes the human voice — subtly, but measurably. The VOICE-DEP study protocol plans multimodal analysis of voice and speech during medical interviews to support the diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring of major depression. The planned research could one day turn an ordinary conversation into a diagnostic instrument.
plos-pone-0356727: Prostate cancer risk stratification desperately needs models doctors can understand. This paper used graph neural networks on gene expression data with SHAP interpretability for risk stratification. The explainable AI sorts patients by risk transparently — showing its reasoning instead of hiding it.
plos-pone-0339427: Does randomization — clinical trials’ gold standard — still make sense when a disease is vanishingly rare? This paper confronted the provocative question head-on. The analysis defends, or dents, the case for randomization precisely where patient numbers make it hardest.
plos-pone-0357127: This entry is a retraction notice, not a research finding. The journal has retracted the paper applying an enhanced Benders decomposition algorithm to circular assembly line balancing with task splitting. The notice formally withdraws those findings from the scientific record.
plos-pone-0354527: Industrial weaving looms need heald frames that are light, stiff, and efficient. This research developed a high-efficiency composite heald frame reinforced with carbon fiber. The advanced frame lets looms run faster with less energy — small part, real productivity gain.
plos-pone-0357027: Gypsum binders can go green. This paper developed sustainable gypsum binders reinforced with industrial and bio-waste additives — turning trash into construction material. The waste-reinforced binders cut the carbon footprint of building without sacrificing performance.
plos-pone-0354727: China’s monetary policy travels through an unusual channel: local government bonds. This paper dissected that transmission mechanism. The findings illuminate how Beijing’s financial levers actually reach — or fail to reach — the real economy through subnational debt markets.
plos-pone-0355727: Drill pipes endure brutal, complex operating conditions — and their connections are the weak link. This paper analyzed performance and structurally optimized drill pipe connections. The optimization promises fewer costly failures deep underground, where a broken connection can doom an entire operation.
plos-pone-0355827: Foreign agricultural land holdings near U.S. military installations raise security eyebrows. This paper mapped their spatial patterns around military interest points. The geographic analysis brings data to a debate often driven by anecdote — showing where foreign farmland actually clusters.
plos-pone-0354927: Spring tomatoes need water and nitrogen in careful balance. This paper tested irrigation lower limits combined with reduced nitrogen plus organic fertilizer on spring-season tomatoes. The findings give growers the recipe for high yields with less water and synthetic fertilizer — a sustainability win.
europmc-pmc2922327: Drug design hinges on molecular grip. This 2010 paper argues tuned water-fearing contacts and hydrogen bonds at the drug-target meeting point lead design paths. The authors' focus sharpens virtual screening. Their work guides better molecular fits. Docking programs that rank drug candidates still use these rules.
europmc-pmc2973827: Zinc can jam coronavirus copying gear. This 2010 paper shows zinc stalls the copy enzymes of coronaviruses and arteriviruses in test tubes, and zinc shuttles halt their growth in cells. The authors spot the jam. Their work hinted at zinc-based virus fighters.
europmc-pmc2993727: Splitting cells into parts can take two minutes. This 2010 paper brings REAP, a two-minute method for splitting cell contents. The authors' speed trick spread through labs. Their method saved countless hours. Grad students wept with joy, reportedly. The trick needs only common lab gear.
europmc-pmc3062527: TB shot policies got mapped worldwide. This 2011 paper builds the BCG World Atlas of global vaccine policies. The authors' database guides TB planners. Their atlas informed programs. Policies differ wildly between countries. The atlas exposes the patchwork plainly. WHO cites it in strategy papers.
europmc-pmc6527027: Alcohol leaves the body through a relay of enzymes - mainly alcohol dehydrogenase, aldehyde dehydrogenase, CYP2E1, and catalase - that convert it step by step into harmless byproducts. This overview explains each stage and why people differ: gene variants make some metabolize alcohol faster or slower, shaping intoxication, hangovers, and long-term risk. The chemistry behind the drink, plainly laid out.
europmc-pmc6537627: Parvoviruses are among the smallest known viruses: rugged, non-enveloped particles carrying just 4-6 thousand bases of single-stranded DNA. This official ICTV taxonomy profile defines the Parvoviridae family, splitting it into viruses of vertebrates and of invertebrates. The reference helps virologists classify new isolates and track a family that includes both harmless passengers and serious pathogens.
europmc-pmc6546127: A typo in DNA can mean a harmless quirk or a serious disease - and doctors need fast answers about which. VarSome is a free search engine for human genetic variants: type in a variant and it aggregates what labs worldwide know, with tools to judge its impact. The community-driven site turns scattered expertise into one shared reference.
europmc-pmc6547727: Many human traits share genetic roots, but simple correlations understate the overlap. MiXeR - a bivariate causal mixture model - measures how much of the genetic signal two traits truly share, beyond what correlation captures. Applied to genome-wide data, the tool reveals hidden connections between complex traits like mental disorders.
europmc-pmc6602427: Most disease mutations sit where proteins touch - and predicting whether a mutation breaks the handshake matters. mCSM-PPI2 is a machine-learning tool that forecasts how single-letter changes alter protein-protein binding. The improved predictor helps geneticists judge which variants are harmful and which are harmless.
europmc-pmc6760227: Sore arms and fevers after shots are not side effects - they are the immune system at work. This review explains vaccine reactogenicity: the hows and whats of the inflammatory response to vaccination. Understanding the racket helps distinguish normal immune noise from real danger.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-27: After years of flu-shot scares, GAO's 2007 report takes the vaccine pipeline apart: how shots get made, how they reach arms, and what the public is told. The supply chain proved brittle, and the health messages did not always land. The report points at the weak links — and asks whether official talk was building trust or burning it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1127: GAO warned Congress in 2007 that the Smithsonian was rotting from the roof down. Leaky tops, tired air systems, and thin guard coverage put the nation's attic — its priceless collections — at risk. The report is a plea to fix the buildings before the treasures inside pay the price of neglect.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-627: The global AIDS fund's books got a review in 2007 — GAO's report says its funding decisions were better documented, with work left to do. The findings credit the progress made. The report's standard is high: billions for the dying deserve bulletproof books.
gao-gaoreports-b-299227: L-3 Communications doubled its March 2007 protest — two case numbers, one fuze-products fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both claims at once. The firm challenged the awards as unfair, and the call weighs each claim with care. Paired filings get one careful answer from the bid court.
openalex-w7204188927: Children are not just adults-in-waiting; they are social actors with their own worlds. This article studies the sociology of childhood and what it offers for understanding atypical childhoods, those lived outside the expected scripts. The authors map contributions, challenges, and new directions. A theoretical piece that takes children's agency seriously.
openalex-w4411194627: Quantum annealers are finicky, and this paper tunes them. The authors studied fixing some qubits' values, with energy rescaling, to help the annealer solve optimization problems despite hardware limits. They measured the performance gains. A quantum-computing study of working smarter within the machine's limits.
openalex-w7163998427: Salty seas may hide tomorrow's antibiotics. This paper reports that salt stress pushed a Streptomyces strain to make 7-deoxypactamycin and oligomycin, two germ-fighting compounds. The team studied how the sea microbe's chemistry woke up under stress. A germ study of pressure unlocking hidden drugs.
openalex-w7163524827: Schizophrenia runs in families, and genes may hold clues. This study tested a set of genes, the inter-alpha-trypsin inhibitors, for links to the disorder. The team hunted DNA hot spots in a strongly inherited illness. A mind-gene study chasing a promising lead.
openalex-w7220678127: Children with malaria only get better if they finish their medicine. This study measured how well caregivers stuck to antimalarial treatment in kids and what the caregivers reported. The authors linked adherence to outcomes. A global-health study of the last mile of malaria care.
openalex-w4416665727: Lincomycin and its kin fight bad infections, and soil germs build them with odd gene kits. This paper sums up new work on how Streptomyces germs make these antibiotics, tracing the strange gene clusters behind them. The authors mapped the field's gains. A review of germ chemistry that saves lives.
openalex-w7214604527: Some blood infections whisper of hidden colon cancer. This paper studied the tie between two germ blood infections and later colon cancer finds. The team probed timing and how it happens. A cancer-germ study of infections as early alarms for tumors.
openalex-w7212146527: After heart surgery, fluid balance is critical. This study tested giving intravenous tolvaptan, a water-shedding drug, right when patients reached the ICU. The team checked whether early dosing was safe and feasible. A cardiac-care study of a new drug's first hours.
pmc-13469727: This 2026 case report describes a patient with Muir–Torre syndrome, a hereditary cancer condition, whose cause was traced to a hidden intronic variant in the MSH2 gene — found only through whole-genome sequencing. The case shows how deep DNA reading can solve mysteries that standard tests miss, changing a family's screening plan.
pmc-13449027: A 2026 Alzheimer's paper testing whether P-tau217 — a phosphorylated tau protein measured in blood — can detect amyloid clearance after treatment with donanemab, an anti-amyloid antibody. A blood test that tracks whether the drug is working would spare patients repeated brain scans. The study evaluates that possibility head-on.
pmc-13435827: In this 2026 population genetics paper, the authors showed that putatively adaptive genetic variation and genome-wide variation often rank populations as similarly distinctive. The finding is a caution: signals of local adaptation may partly reflect the same structure as neutral variation. It urges care in reading selection from DNA.
pmc-13428227: A 2026 study exploring how sleep difficulties interact with anxiety, depression, and quality of life in pulmonary hypertension — high blood pressure in the lungs. The condition disrupts sleep, and poor sleep worsens everything else. Untangling the web points to where treatment helps most.
pmc-13386027: A 2026 physiology paper showing that disrupting claudin-2 and TRPV6 — proteins controlling calcium transport — causes low blood calcium, high urinary calcium, and altered bone microarchitecture in mice. The double disruption reveals how the gut and kidney coordinate calcium balance. The bone changes underscore calcium's structural stakes.
pmc-13472727: A 2026 computational biology paper on faster inference of complex demographic models from large allele frequency spectra — the patterns of genetic variation that record population history. Speed matters as datasets grow to millions of genomes. The method accelerates a core population-genetics task.
pmc-13243727: In this 2026 neuroscience paper, female mice showed stronger time-of-day modulation of astrocytic calcium activity in the sleep-regulatory ventrolateral preoptic nucleus. The brain's sleep center pulses differently across the day in females. The sex difference is the headline.
pmc-13546927: A 2026 Indian multicentric survey comparing mortality and therapy costs of carbapenem-susceptible versus resistant Gram-negative infections in hospitalized patients. Resistance kills and bankrupts. The survey quantifies both tolls.
pmc-13467527: A 2026 materials paper on wear behavior of 316L stainless steel plates made by wire arc additive manufacturing. 3D-printed metal wears differently. The study characterizes it.
pmc-13431427: A 2026 retrospective study using the eICU database on 28-day mortality and prognostic factors in COPD patients with sepsis. The critically ill lung patients' outcomes were modeled. The factors inform ICU care.
pmc-13587827: A 2026 study using metabolomic analysis of gingival crevicular fluid for dental age and skeletal maturity assessment in growing individuals. Gum fluid metabolites marked development. The analysis offers a non-invasive age tool.
pmc-13490627: This 2026 drug discovery paper used ligand-based virtual screening to find thienopyrimidinone derivatives as allosteric nSMase2 modulators and antivirals against West Nile virus. The computational hits were the leads. The screening is the pipeline.
pmc-13477227: In this 2026 neuroscience paper, oligodendrocyte and astrocyte dynamics during short-term cuprizone treatment were tracked. The demyelination model's glia were watched. The dynamics inform multiple sclerosis research.
pmc-13464827: In this 2026 food chemistry paper, preparation-route-associated differences in color and non-volatile metabolite profiles of Eurotium cristatum-fermented fu tea were studied. The dark tea's chemistry varied by method. The profiles are the finding.
pmc-13422127: A 2026 comparative biochemical study of oleate hydratases. The fatty acid enzymes were compared. The study is the enzymology.
pmc-13411027: A 2026 study of dietary and lifestyle changes before and after cardiovascular disease diagnosis. The diagnosis prompted behavior change. The changes are the data.
pmc-13369527: A 2026 correction notice for a CFIR-informed exploration of a primary care intervention to support deprescribing (the title is truncated). Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13332427: A 2026 critical care paper comparing clinical pneumonia assessments to bronchoalveolar lavage results in critically ill patients with suspected pneumonia. The bedside judgment was checked against the lavage. The comparison reveals the diagnostic gap.
pmc-13473827: A 2026 review on endocrine regulation of cardiac fibrosis — implications for HFpEF. The hormone-heart scarring link was surveyed. The implications are the therapeutic angle.
pmc-13521527: This 2026 in vitro study evaluated cytotoxicity, setting time, and mineralization potential of mineral trioxide aggregate with Nigella sativa aqueous extract (the title is truncated). The black seed-enhanced dental cement was tested. The evaluation is the evidence.
pmc-13428127: In this 2026 case report, papillary renal neoplasm with reverse polarity was described. The unusual kidney tumor was characterized. The case documents the entity.
pmc-13550427: A 2026 paper on reliability of short-term heart rate variability measurements in patients with non-permanent atrial fibrillation. The HRV's reliability was tested. The reliability informs monitoring.
pmc-13463927: A 2026 study of balance training distribution effects on balance performance in adolescents. The training schedule mattered. The effects inform coaching.
arxiv-2606-16027: A math paper about shapes cut out by math rules called polynomial equations. 'Blow-up' tricks zoom in on the rough spots of a shape to grasp them, and the paper uses them on Segre classes and multidegree formulas — tools that count how shapes cross. It is for pure math pros.
arxiv-2606-16227: Light combs — lasers that spit a rainbow of matched hues — are lab jewels. This paper dreams them up on sky scales: 'cosmo combs,' and charts the wild swings such sky combs might fall into. A what-if that links laser lore with deep-space lore, for theory fans.
arxiv-2606-16327: Acoustic-to-articulatory inversion means figuring out how the tongue and lips moved just from recorded speech — but real articulatory data is scarce. ArtBoost creates synthetic articulatory data to augment the real stuff, giving models more to learn from. The paper targets speech researchers building systems that infer vocal-tract movement from audio.
arxiv-2606-16627: A pure mathematics paper on multiple zeta-star values — exotic numbers built from infinite sums that generalize the famous zeta function. It studies their divided differences and complex variations: how these numbers shift and deform. It is for number theorists.
arxiv-2606-16827: Most code AI learns from Python and JavaScript — but what about rare tongues with no test sets? This paper tests and lifts LLMs for code-making in 'no-resource' tongues. It is for teams bringing AI code help to under-served languages.
